summary: Tenant-aware batcher weight update loop causing p95/p99 spikes for short streaming requests
description:
Issue summary:
BrightHealth AI reported repeated p95/p99 latency spikes and intermittent 504s for short streaming requests (single-turn generation, ~10-30 tokens). Spikes began after a deployment to a Dedicated cluster on 2026-03-09 and are most visible during morning traffic ramp (08:00-10:30 US-EAST).

Impact:
- Several customer endpoints experienced 10-30x p99 increases for short streams, causing user-facing timeouts in production workflows.
- Error surfaces: intermittent 504s and timeouts reported from SDK and HTTP clients.
- Affects BrightHealth AI (dedicated) primarily; small signal seen from other dedicated tenants sharing the same GPU pool.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (gpu-pool-dedicated-us-east-3)
- Serving runtime version: 2.14.0+arc-20260308
- Batcher component: continuous-batcher v1.9.3 with tenant-weighting feature enabled
- KV-cache: cold-to-warm transitions observed during traffic ramp

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start short streaming workload (1 concurrent connection per client, bursts of ~50 qps across tenant).
2) After cache-priming burst, contiguous requests experience periodic p99 spikes lasting 10-30s.
3) Spikes correlate with a sequence of batcher weight updates and high pending-queue depth for several microbatches.

Observed behavior:
- p95 remains largely stable; p99 and tail latency jump intermittently to several seconds.
- Traces show increased queuing time inside the continuous-batcher queue and multiple re-enqueue/reweight cycles for tenant slots.
- KV-cache hit-rate dips during spike windows (warmup activity), which aligns with increased batch formation time.

Expected behavior:
- Stable p95/p99 for short streaming requests outside of full-queue saturation. Batcher should adjust weights without creating re-enqueue loops or widening latency tail.

Logs & traces:
- Sample trace: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/6f8d2b10 (shows re-enqueue loops and 3x queue attempts)
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency/dedicated-batcher?orgId=1&from=2026-03-10T07:30:00Z&to=2026-03-10T11:00:00Z
- Error excerpts: 
  - "queue_wait_ms: 2187, batch_attempts: 4, tenant_weight_update: true"
  - "kv_cache_miss_ratio: 0.62 during spike window"

Investigation summary (see investigation_notes for details):
- Early signs point to an interaction between tenant-specific batcher weight recalculation and KV-cache warmup behavior.
- Weight updates temporarily reduce flush thresholds for some tenant slots, causing many short streams to be coalesced into slightly larger microbatches; when KV-cache warmup increases per-request processing time, the batcher sees growing queue depth and triggers additional weight adjustments, creating a short feedback loop that amplifies tail latency.

Customer-facing notes:
- Notified BrightHealth AI support contact (Maria Gonzalez) on 2026-03-10 09:05 UTC with temporary mitigation steps.
- We advised increased client-side retry/backoff and enabling the tenant-specific 'short-stream-priority' flag as a short-term mitigation.

Resolution status:
- Mitigation (hotfix) deployed 2026-03-11 02:20 UTC: temporary disablement of tenant-weight auto-ramp and application of a conservative max-linger cap for dedicated gpu-pool-dedicated-us-east-3.
- Observed immediate reduction of p99 spikes after hotfix; monitoring in progress.

investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC: Serving runtime and continuous-batcher rollout (v2.14.0+arc-20260308).
- 2026-03-10 07:20 UTC: First alerts for p99 spikes on BrightHealth AI tenant.
- 2026-03-10 08:10-10:30 UTC: Repro window during morning ramp; correlates with KV-cache misses and increased batch_attempts metric.
- Metrics examined: queue_wait_ms, batch_attempts, tenant_weight_update_events, kv_cache_miss_ratio, avg_batch_size.
- Key observation: tenant_weight_update_events spike ~1-2s before p99 jump in multiple traces. Weight recalculation algorithm increases allocation for tenants showing higher pending request counts; that increase lowered flush thresholds and increased coalescing for short streams, which interacted poorly with transient KV-cache warmup latency.
- Re-enqueue loop: when a microbatch is delayed due to longer per-request execution (cache miss), the batcher recalculates weights and may reassign slots causing the same requests to be re-enqueued into newly formed microbatches, counting as additional batch_attempts and amplifying queue time.
- Repro recipe locally: simulate kv-cache miss delay (~120-250ms per request) + enable tenant-weight auto-ramp + short stream traffic pattern -> reproduce p99 spikes within 30s.
- Tested mitigation locally: limiting weight_update frequency to 1 per 10s and max-linger cap for short streams eliminated the loop and returned p99 to baseline.
resolution_notes:
Hotfix details (2026-03-11 02:20 UTC):
- Disabled tenant-weight auto-ramp for gpu-pool-dedicated-us-east-3 cluster.
- Added conservative max-linger cap for streams with token length < 40 for dedicated pools.
- Added temporary monitoring alert: tenant_weight_update_rate > 5/min + kv_cache_miss_ratio > 0.5 triggers pager.

Customer outcome:
- BrightHealth AI reported restoration of normal latency profile within 5-10 minutes of hotfix.
- Continued monitoring for 24-72 hours; no recurrence observed in initial window.

Permanent fix proposal (in progress):
1) Add KV-cache-awareness to weight recalculation: suppress or dampen weight updates during detected warmup windows.
2) Prioritize short-streams path in coalescer so they are less likely to be re-enqueued.
3) Add unit/integration tests to CI that simulate weight updates during cache warmup to prevent regressions.
4) Roll out phased change with canary on non-production pools.

Follow-up tasks created: INT-3341 (postmortem), INT-3342 (CI test), INT-3343 (weighting algorithm redesign).
